reply_text:
Found two issues in `receipt-lines` against `main`:

1. **[P1] Printed amounts are 100× too large** — `receipt/render.py:2`  
   `format_money` formats cents directly as dollars: `format_money(1299)` returns `$1299.00`, not `$12.99`. Two coffees at 450 cents print `$900.00` instead of `$9.00`. Convert cents to dollars before formatting. The current test misses this because it builds its expected suffix using the same broken formatter; assert literal dollar strings instead.

2. **[P2] Right-alignment isn’t applied to printed lines** — `receipt/render.py:7`  
   `render_line` still uses a fixed 20-character name field rather than the new `layout.align` helper. Amounts start at the same column but end at different columns as their digit counts change, so they aren’t right-aligned to the 32-column receipt. Use the alignment helper and test rendered lines with different-length amounts.

All **3 existing tests pass**, but they don’t catch these issues. I’d fix the money conversion before merging. No files changed.
